decisions.reason: The firm has invested heavily in this water phantom for the growing particle therapy segment and publicly announced its Q1/2019 release, so the commitment is visible and strategic and withdrawal is very unlikely.

Small volume chambers are central to the firm's dosimetry portfolio for small-field radiotherapy, and a new product with its own page will be given time to build sales over typical clinical adoption cycles.

Although it overlaps with the other small volume chamber, it was launched recently and is publicly presented, so management will attribute any slow uptake to temporary adoption delays rather than drop it.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is a core reference product for the firm's established customer base, and the investment and certification behind it make retention near certain.
Relative dosimetry chambers complement the firm's water phantoms and scanning systems, so the product fits the announced system strategy and will be retained.
Thimble chambers are a staple of the dosimetry range, and with recent launch costs and regulatory effort sunk, the firm will persist with the product.
